issues.situation: It never fires in the bench. I checked the three fixture saves (~/.local/share/godot/app_userdata/40k/saves/{mirror_custodes_2000,asym_2000,mirror_orks_2000}_postdeploy.w40ksave): none has attached leaders, reserves or embarked units. The plan is built once per Movement phase (AIDecisionMaker.gd @12e0753:6835-6899). Gate (a)'s 'locked' OC is friendly_oc minus the OC of the movable candidates on the objective (10087-10095). In the bench that leaves only one source: an engaged unit standing on a held_threatened objective with need 0, beating max(enemy, projected) while a movable co-holder is also there. Gate (b) needs a same-phase swap won only on spare inches (every bench Custodes unit is M6, Allarus M5) onto an objective with 0 enemy OC in range and none within M+2" (17.8" for the Ork M12 units). The designer measured 0 fires in 8 full bench games (6 Custodes mirror, 2 asym) and did not run the Ork mirror. Protocol v2 needs at least 1.0 tag line per game, i.e. 6 or more in the 6-game reach run. This design would be PARKED, and the benchmark would replay identical games and could not show a gain.
issues.proposed_change: Do not ship it; at most park it with FIX_MARGINAL_OC default 0. No small tweak of these two gates reaches the bench. A rule that does reach it would have to act on the case the bench actually produces: several movable units pinned on one held_threatened objective with need 0 (the 'holding under threat' decision type). In pass 1, hold those units in OBJ-HOLD-2 keeper-key order only until locked non-engaged OC plus their own OC (attached leaders included) exceeds enemy_oc + projected_enemy_oc, and release the rest to pass 2. That is a new design: it needs its own reach run, guardrail replays and horizon-2 checks before any bench.

issues.situation: Gate (a)'s only flip, s7475 r3 P1, is a replay artifact built on miscounted OC. In 40k/tests/rollout_cases/r5c00/s7475_r3_p1_movement_2.w40ksave, P1's 20 OC on obj_center (the 11e hosting area is the two centre ruins) is Guard B 9 + Guard C 9 + Blade Champion C 2, and Blade Champion C is attached to Guard B. Guard C is not engaged: its nearest enemy base is 2.03" away and 11e engagement range is 2" (GameConstants.gd:32-33). It had simply already acted this phase (flags moved + remained_stationary). The real game built its plan at phase start with Guard C still movable, so locked OC = 20 - 18 = 2 < threat 9. Gate (a) would not fire and Guard B would hold exactly as on the base. Only the rollout re-plans mid-phase (a fresh process; the save holds no turn_movement_plan) and sees 'locked 11'. Even then, 2 of those 11 are Guard B's own Blade Champion, which moves with it: MovementPhase.gd:7806 gives attached characters no move row, and _unit_alive_oc counts only the bodyguard's models. RI-QUARTER (10005-10015) already removes attached leaders; locked_oc_holds does not. True locked OC is 9, which only ties the enemy's 9, and the enemy can stand there with enemy_oc + projected = 9 + 7 = 16 next turn. The gate uses max() = 9, while the shipped RI-RACE uses the sum (9640-9642). So the rule's premise is false at its own evidence: Guard B's move paid because flipping obj_nml_1 was worth more, not because the centre was safe. In real games the AI attaches every Blade Champion, and the miscount produces a concrete harmful case. Two Guard squads, each with its Champion, hold an objective (P2's home in s7489 has 19 OC laid out this way) and one weakened enemy unit with OC 3 or less is within 12". Locked = 4 (the two Champions) > threat 3, so both squads are released, the Champions leave with them, 0 OC is left and the enemy walks on. On the base both squads hold. The bench has no attachments and cannot see this. The same miscount already exists in base KEEP-OC on held_safe objectives; that is a separate defect.
issues.proposed_change: Drop gate (a). If it is kept: (i) add each movable candidate's attached characters' in-range OC to movable_oc_on_obj, using the same loop as RI-QUARTER at 10009; (ii) compare locked OC with enemy_oc + projected_enemy_oc instead of max(); (iii) do not count engaged or SCREEN-earmarked units (9496-9506) as locked. With (i) and (ii) the gate does not fire at s7475 even in the replay. Record s7475 as not addressed rather than ship a gate that fires for the wrong reason.

issues.situation: Gate (a) treats an engaged unit's OC as guaranteed, but it is the least reliable OC on the board. The unit fights in our Fight phase and again in the enemy turn before we next score. _decide_engaged_unit (11199+) also runs after the plan is built. In rounds 2-3, with a lethal survival estimate, it falls back when 'others can hold' (11295-11297). That count still includes the co-holder the plan has just released, because engaged units act first and the co-holder is still standing there. Both leave. This repeats round 3's REINFORCE-CAP failure: holders that leave the objective were missing from the count. The same path can release a home holder while the home objective is in melee.
issues.proposed_change: Leave engaged units out of gate (a)'s locked OC. Alternatively, count one only from battle round 4 (when _decide_engaged_unit keeps it, 11274) and only when _assess_engaged_unit_survival is not lethal.

issues.situation: Gate (b) has no limit on the OC gap and never checks that the bigger unit can actually reach its 'contested' alternative. The evidence is a gap of 1 (Guard 9 vs Prosecutors 8). In the bench Custodes roster, Blade Champions are standalone single models with OC 2. If the gate fires with a Champion as the greedy pick, one OC-2 model becomes the only capturer of an objective that the enemy can reach in two moves (the gate looks only at enemy OC in range and one move away). Meanwhile the OC-10 Guard is sent to an alternative that the patch's mo_c loop checks only for state and remaining need. That alternative may then be skipped by DIM-RETURNS, TOO-LATE, RACE-SKIP or LONE-TRIP, and the Guard ends up in the support pass. A one-round rollout cannot see this cost in rounds 3-5.
issues.proposed_change: Skip the swap only when alt.unit_oc - cand.unit_oc <= 2, or when cand's OC alone beats the enemy's two-move race OC at that objective (enemy_arrivals with moves <= cand phases + 1). Also require the alt's alternative candidate to pass reprice_capture (no skip), too_late, race_hopeless and lone_trip, with turns_to_reach <= cand_arrival.phases.

issues.situation: In a real game the design changes only one finding, s7478 r3 P2 (gate b). The swap there does not depend on the two P2 units that had already acted, so it probably also flips outside the replay. That finding has not confirmed at horizon 2: a partial result is already logged in .ai_lab_work/STATUS.md at 03:34 (pr12h2_9: +4.54 [-4.49, 13.57] for the centre move). The fix's own choice there (obj_nml_1) has only 8 seeds at horizon 1 (+9.13 [1.18, 17.07]). s7463, the finding with the most seeds, is not addressed. The report's '2/3 flipped' should read 1/3 in real play.
issues.proposed_change: Report coverage as 1/3 (s7478 only). Hold any decision on gate (b) until s7478 (obj_nml_1) has horizon-2 numbers, and park it (FIX param 0) if they do not confirm.

reviews.fires_in_bench: About 0 per game (my estimate is 0 to 0.3 pooled). The designer measured 0 fires in 8 full bench games (3 Custodes-mirror pairs and 1 asym pair) and did not run the Ork mirror. The reasons are structural. The three fixture saves have no attached leaders, no reserves and no embarked units (I checked each), and the plan is built once per Movement phase, so mid-phase replans almost never happen. Gate (a)'s 'locked' OC can then only be an engaged unit on a held_threatened objective with need 0 that still beats max(enemy, projected) while a movable co-holder stands there too. That is uncommon: the Ork M12-14 units make projected OC large, and Custodes centre fights usually have more enemy units within 11.8". A few fires are possible in the Ork mirror after round-1 Waaagh charges onto objectives. Gate (b) needs a same-phase swap won only on spare inches (every bench Custodes unit is M6, Allarus M5) onto an objective with 0 enemy OC in range and none within M+2" (17.8" for Ork bikes), plus a contested alternative for the bigger unit. Either way this is well below the v2 fix gate of 1.0 per game (6 or more tag lines in the 6-game reach run), so the design would be PARKED and bench pairs would play out identically.
reviews.strengths: It is the smallest possible change. It sits fully behind its parameter (0 restores the base exactly), both gates log the same tag, and it ships with a unit test that fails on the base. It leaves all 7 guardrails alone, and also the late s7489 r1 P1 Mek reinforcement: the support pass that writes 'already committed' is untouched, and at that position (I checked the save) P1 has no contested, enemy-held or threatened objective, so neither gate can fire. Gate (b) correctly leaves whole-turn-quicker swaps alone (guardrail s7457), and it probably changes s7478 in a real game as well, not just in the replay. The report is candid: it states 0 bench reach itself, says s7463 is not fixed, and names the engaged-holder and home-objective risks.
reviews.summary: Verdict: drop. This is from reading code and save files only; I ran no games. The design adds two narrow gates to existing overrides. In the bench it is effectively inert: the fixtures have no attached leaders, reserves or transports, and the designer measured 0 fires in 8 full games. It therefore fails the protocol-v2 fix gate, and the bench would replay identical games. Gate (a)'s flip at s7475 does not hold up. It appears only because the rollout re-plans mid-phase: Guard C was not engaged (2.03" from the nearest enemy, against a 2" range) and had already acted, so at the real phase-start plan locked OC is 2 against a threat of 9 and Guard B holds as on the base. The 'locked OC 11' seen in the replay also includes Guard B's own attached Blade Champion. The true locked OC of 9 only ties the enemy's 9, and loses to enemy_oc + projected = 16, which is the sum the shipped RI-RACE uses. The rule's premise is false at its own evidence; the move paid off because obj_nml_1 was worth more, not because the centre was safe. In real games, where the AI attaches every Champion, the same miscount can release every holder of a threatened objective. For example, two Guard+Champion squads facing one weakened enemy unit both walk off, and the bench cannot see that regression. Counting engaged units as locked adds risk on top: they fight twice before we next score and can fall back while counting on the co-holder that was just released. Gate (b) is a plausible narrow rule and does change s7478 in a real game. But it puts no limit on the OC gap (in the bench a lone OC-2 Champion could be left as an objective's only capturer), it does not check that the bigger unit can actually take its alternative, and s7478 did not confirm at horizon 2 (+4.54 [-4.49, 13.57]). Nothing here should ship. At most, park gate (b) behind FIX_MARGINAL_OC = 0 with the gap limit added. Separately, base KEEP-OC already has the same attached-leader miscount on held_safe objectives; that defect shows only in real games, never in the bench.

issues.situation: Gate (a) frees the unit on a false count. At s7475 r3 P1, P1's 20 OC on obj_center is Guard Gamma 9 (already acted this phase), Guard Beta 9 and Blade Champion Gamma 2. Decoding the save shows the Blade Champion's attached_to is U_CUSTODIAN_GUARD_B. The gate (patched AIDecisionMaker.gd:10156, through locked_oc_holds at :10107) computes 20 - 9 = 11 > maxi(9, 7) and frees Beta. The engine does not give attached characters their own move (MovementPhase.get_available_actions skips attached_to; _move_attached_characters moves them with the bodyguard). So only 9 OC stays against the 9 enemy OC already in range, a tie with no control. After P2's move the enemy can have 9 + 7 = 16 there. maxi() was harmless in base KEEP-OC because held_safe objectives have enemy_oc 0. The gate now applies it where the enemy is already in range. In real games with leaders the same count frees a holder whose departure loses the objective at once. Example: Guard 9 + attached Champion 2 + engaged Allarus 6 vs enemy 7 leaves 6 vs 7.
issues.proposed_change: Use a gate-only count and leave the base KEEP-OC helper as it is, so param 0 stays exact. From the locked OC, also subtract the in-range OC of every character attached to a movable unit already on the objective, and of units withheld by a SCREEN earmark. Compare the result with enemy_oc + projected_enemy_oc (the threat LONE-TRIP uses), not maxi(). With this change s7475 no longer fires, so the report must stop claiming that finding.

issues.situation: The s7475 decision change only happens because the replay starts mid-phase. COORD-4 builds the movement plan once, at the first unit decision of the phase, and reuses it (test_ai_battle_plan checks there is no re-plan between unit actions). The s7475 save's phase_log shows Guard Gamma's REMAIN_STATIONARY already carried the plan entry 'hold obj_center (holding under threat (enemy OC 9 nearby))'. So the plan was built while Gamma and Beta could both move: movable OC 18, locked OC 2, and gate (a) cannot fire. In a continuous game Beta follows the stored plan and holds, exactly as on base. The rollout loads the save with an empty plan cache and re-plans after Gamma has acted, which is the only reason the decision check shows 'changed: true'. The report's root cause is also wrong. Gamma was not engaged (flags moved + remained_stationary, no in_engagement), and the 'Blade Champion' counted as locked is Beta's own attached leader.
issues.proposed_change: Re-run the decision check from the start of P1's round-3 Movement phase, or with two _decide_movement calls on the same snapshot as test_ai_battle_plan does. Report that gate (a) does not address s7475 in real play. Making it work would mean re-checking the not-yet-acted holders in the stored plan after each unit acts, which is a larger design. Otherwise remove gate (a).

issues.situation: The fix has almost no reach in the bench. The 3 fixtures have 0 attached leaders, 0 embarked units and no reserves (decoded), and the plan is built at the start of each phase. So gate (a)'s locked OC can only come from our engaged units, or Allarus returning via On Gilded Wings. It then also needs need 0, locked OC above the threat, and a second non-engaged unit on the same objective. Gate (b) needs a rare swap pattern. The designer measured 0 fires in 8 games and did not play the Orks mirror. Protocol v2 needs at least 1.0 fire per game, so the fix would be parked.
issues.proposed_change: No change inside this design raises reach. Play the Orks-mirror pair before any decision. Otherwise treat it as parked or dropped.

issues.situation: Gate (b) accepts any candidate of the quicker unit at a contested, enemy_weak or held_threatened objective that still needs OC. That includes candidates pass 2 then skips (TOO-LATE, RACE-SKIP, LONE-TRIP, FAR-TRIP, DIM-RETURNS) and 3-4 turn trips. In the unit test's own swap board, the Guard's obj_2 candidate is about 34.6" away. When pass 2 skips that target, the bigger unit is refused the swap and lands in the support fallback, while the smaller unit takes the uncontested objective.
issues.proposed_change: Require mo_c to pass the same checks pass 2 applies: not reprice_capture(mo_c.objective_id).skip, not too_late, race_hopeless, lone_trip or far_trip. Also require int(mo_c.turns_to_reach) <= cand_arrival.phases + 1.

issues.situation: Gate (b) treats an objective as uncontestable from enemy_oc == 0 and projected_enemy_oc == 0, which look only one enemy move ahead. Its main case is a 2-phase arrival (s7478: 2 vs 2), so the enemy gets more moves before the unit arrives and scores. Round 3's REINFORCE-CAP was dropped for this kind of short-sighted threat count.
issues.proposed_change: When cand_arrival.phases > 1, also require int(cand.get("race_enemy_oc", 0)) == 0. Candidates already carry this race value for multi-turn trips.

issues.situation: At s7478, gate (b) sends Beta to obj_nml_1, not to the measured obj_center. The Prosecutors walk home, so the centre gets 8 OC less reinforcement than on base. The only evidence for this choice is n8 +9.13 [1.18, 17.07] at horizon 1.
issues.proposed_change: Measure the fix's own choice over 24 seeds and at horizon 2 before counting s7478 as fixed.

issues.situation: The test pins the fix on and erases the override. It fails on base for the right reason and drives _assign_units_to_objectives, as the other fix tests do. It is missing cases: an attached leader on the movable holder (this would expose the first major issue), an enemy in range plus projected OC (sum vs max), negative gate-(b) cases (projected > 0, or no control-changing option, so the swap still happens), and the KEEP-OC-ablated branch. Because it calls the assignment function directly, it cannot show the plan-persistence effect behind the second major issue.
issues.proposed_change: Add those cases. Add one two-call _decide_movement test with the s7475 shape (one holder acts after the plan is built) that asserts what the fix does in a continuous game.

issues.situation: Code comments, log and constant placement. The comment says the unit 'falls through to the keeper / KEEP-OC checks', but the elif chain ends at the new branch: it hard-codes the KEEP-OC outcome and skips AGGRO-FREE and KEEPER-RELEASE. The [MARGINAL_OC] line is printed even when the keeper is then held (KEEP-OC ablated). The FIX_MARGINAL_OC block sits inside the REINFORCE-INSURANCE constants, between RI_QUARTER_LATER_ROUND_SHARE and RI_RACE_LOST_RATIO.
issues.proposed_change: Correct the comment. Print the line only when should_hold stays false. Move the constant block below RI_RACE_LOST_RATIO.

issues.situation: The report leaves out two guardrails: s7451 r1 P2 (the 7th guardrail in the cluster) was not replayed, and the extra s7489 r1 P1 Mek reinforcement was not checked. From the code, neither gate touches them: s7489 comes from the support fallback ('reinforcing obj_center (1 unit already committed)'), and s7451 is a plain capture, not a swap. No change is expected, but no replay confirms it.
issues.proposed_change: Replay both guardrails with the fix on.

reviews.fires_in_bench: Estimate: about 0 to 0.3 [MARGINAL_OC] lines per game, with most games at 0. That is far below the protocol-v2 fix gate of at least 1.0 per game. The designer measured 0 in 8 bench games (3 Custodes-mirror pairs and 1 asym pair, all identical); the Orks mirror was not played. Reasons, from the code and the decoded fixtures: the 3 fixtures have no attached leaders, no embarked units and nothing in reserve. The COORD-4 plan is therefore built once at the start of each Movement phase, while every unit not engaged can still move. Gate (a)'s 'locked' OC then comes only from our engaged units on the objective, or from Custodes Allarus returning through On Gilded Wings. It also needs a held_threatened objective with need 0, where that locked OC alone beats both the enemy OC in range and the enemy OC one move away, plus a second unit on the same objective that is not engaged. The fires seen in the designer's replays (s7475, s7479) came from mid-phase re-plans or from sweep games with leaders or reserves, which the bench does not have. Gate (b) needs an OBJ-ASSIGN-1 swap where both units arrive in the same number of phases, the quicker one has at least 3\" more spare move and MORE OC, the objective has no enemy OC in range or one move away, and the quicker unit has a contested or enemy-held candidate. In the Orks fixture the quick M12 units mostly have less OC than the slow ones, and M12 enemy reach makes 'projected 0' rare. In the Custodes fixture (M5-6) a Guard/Allarus vs Prosecutors/Blade Champion swap is possible but uncommon.
reviews.strengths: Setting FIX_MARGINAL_OC to 0 gives exactly the base behaviour. Both changed paths are behind marginal_oc_on, the existing held_threatened clause is kept unchanged after the new elif, and no debug log line is removed. Each gate is one condition on an existing override and costs almost nothing: gate (b)'s inner loop over candidates only runs for the rare alternative that passes every swap filter. The code is safe on empty data (dictionary .get calls with defaults, _get_obj_eval_by_id returns {}), and the format strings match their arguments. Gate (b) is a sound narrow idea, and it does work in a continuous game at s7478: the swap came from the plan built at the start of the phase, and the inputs gate (b) checks are the same there. Neither gate touches the support-fallback reinforcement at s7489, the keeper holds at s7468 and s7490, or the swap one whole turn quicker at s7457. The test pins the fix on and erases the override, fails on base for the right reason (the forced hold and the swap), and includes guard cases: a needed holder still holds, a swap one whole turn quicker still happens, and param 0 restores base. The report is open about 0 bench fires and lists real risks.
reviews.summary:
Verdict: drop. I did not run Godot (read-only review). Everything below comes from reading the patched AI and engine code and decoding the saved positions and bench fixtures.

The parameter gating is exact, and the code is clean and cheap. The problem is gate (a), which carries the design's main claim (s7475). It does not do what the report says:

1. **It fires there only because of a wrong count.** `locked_oc_holds` treats Blade Champion Gamma as unable to move, but it is attached to Beta and the engine moves it with Beta. It also takes the threat as maxi(9, 7) instead of 9 + 7. The true picture is 9 OC staying against 9 enemy OC now (a tie, so no control) and up to 16 enemy OC after P2's move. The same count can lose an objective at once in real games with leaders.
2. **The decision change only exists in the mid-phase replay.** The movement plan is built once, at the start of the phase, and the save shows it already held Gamma as a planned holder. At that point Gamma and Beta could both move, the locked OC was 2, and Beta holds exactly as on base. The report's root cause ('Guard Gamma engaged') is also wrong: Gamma had stood still earlier in the same phase and was not engaged.

So in real play the design changes at most 1 of the 3 findings: s7478, through gate (b). There Beta goes to obj_nml_1, not to the measured obj_center, and that choice has only 8 seeds of evidence. s7463 is not addressed.

Bench reach is close to zero. The fixtures have no leaders and no reserves, and the plan is built at the start of each phase, so neither gate's trigger arises often. The designer measured 0 fires in 8 games, which protocol v2 would park.

If anything is kept, keep gate (b) alone, parked, with tighter checks: the target objective must pass the same skip checks pass 2 uses, and for trips of 2+ phases the enemy race OC must be 0.

issues.situation: Part (a) at its own evidence position, s7475 r3 P1. The same applies to any held_threatened objective where the released holder has an attached leader. I rebuilt objective control from the save (r5c00/s7475_r3_p1_movement_2.w40ksave) with the engine's hosting-area test (MissionManager._model_in_objective_range: the base overlaps the area-trapezoid polygons). It matches the designer's log exactly. obj_center: friendly 20 = Custodian Guard Beta 9 + its attached Blade Champion C 2 + Custodian Guard Gamma 9. Enemy 9 in range (CG Alpha P2 6 + CG Gamma P2 3). Projected 7 (Blade Champion B P2 2 + Blade Champion C P2 2 + CG Beta P2 3). _marginal_oc_holder_surplus subtracts only cand.unit_oc, which is _unit_alive_oc(unit) (base line 12262): the bodyguard's own models. The attached Blade Champion is a separate unit, so it is in friendly_oc. It cannot move on its own (MovementPhase.gd:610 'Attached character moves with its bodyguard unit'), so it leaves with Beta. The real number that stays is 9, which only TIES the 9 enemy OC in range (contested; 14.02 needs strictly more). The rule fires here only because of this error ('11 stays > 9'). The stated root cause, 'Beta's OC changed nothing there', is also false. Beta's unit takes the centre from held 20-9 to contested 9-9, with 7 more enemy OC one move away. So the measured +8.0 comes from trading control of the centre to flip obj_nml_1, not from surplus OC. In real games the AI attaches all three Blade Champions to Custodian Guard squads (see the save's DECLARE_LEADER_ATTACHMENT history). There, (a) as written will release bodyguards and leave held_threatened objectives tied or lost. The bench fixtures have leader_attachments {}, so the bench cannot show this cost.
issues.proposed_change: Count the released OC as the unit's in-range OC plus the in-range OC of each unit in attachment_data.attached_characters (_unit_oc_at_position for each component). Use that value in both _marginal_oc_holder_surplus and moc_freed_oc, and add a unit test with an attached leader. After this fix s7475 holds (9 > 9 is false), so (a) has no measured finding left. Do not ship (a) without new evidence for a release where the OC really is surplus. Side note: base KEEP-OC has the same gap: movable_oc_on_obj at line 10087 leaves out attached leaders, so a bodyguard's own leader reads as 'locked' OC. That is worth a separate audit; I have not verified it in play.

issues.situation:
Part (b) blocks a same-phase OBJ-ASSIGN-1 swap whenever alt OC > max(greedy OC, need). That includes the case where the greedy pick cannot cover the need (greedy OC < need < alt OC). In that case the alt's OC is not surplus. The greedy pick is committed, the need stays open, and pass 2 usually still sends the alt (its score is within MOVE_ASSIGN_CLOSER_MARGIN of the greedy pick's) or another unit. The result is one more unit stacked on that objective, mostly in round 1. In this container's session logs this is the main shape (counts use the greedy pick's OC from the same movement phase):
- 5 of 5 fires in 16 older bench-like Custodes-mirror full games, all in round 1. Example: CG Alpha P2 OC 10 swapped in for Blade Champion Alpha OC 2, need 6, a 3-turn race to obj_center; in the base the Champion fell through to a support move. TOO-LATE in V10 would remove the two 6-turn cases.
- 66 of 69 in older full sweep games.
- 7 of 15 in V10-era rollouts.
- The one V10-era bench-army game, a reserve smoke game, round 1: Deffkoptas OC 12 vs Warbikers OC 2, need 11.
The evidence case s7478 has the other shape (Prosecutors OC 8 vs need 1). Even there the fix sends CG Beta P2 on a 2-turn trip to obj_nml_1. The measured alternative was a Normal move to obj_center (P1 holds it 13 vs 11; Beta with its attached Blade Champion adds 11). The STATUS.md log shows that alternative's horizon-2 re-check did not confirm: +4.54 [-4.49, 13.57].
issues.proposed_change: Block the swap only when the greedy pick alone covers the need: add `and int(cand.unit_oc) >= remaining` to the (b) condition. Preferably drop (b). With that condition it fired in 0 of the 16 bench-like games, and its only finding is flipped to an unmeasured destination.

issues.situation: Bench reach under the protocol v2 fix gate (>= 1.0 [MARGINAL_OC] line per game over 1 pair per fixture). The designer's only pair (Custodes mirror, seed 93101) gave 1 line in 2 games: Prosecutors released from obj_home_1. Both games ended -53 with 681 actions, so the release changed no action. My estimate across the 3 fixtures is 0.3-0.7 lines per game (see fires_in_bench). The corrections above add no bench fires (the bench has no attached leaders) and remove most of (b)'s fires.
issues.proposed_change: Do not spend a bench run on it. Keep FIX_MARGINAL_OC = 0 (park) unless a redesigned trigger first shows >= 1.0 fires per game in the 6-game reach run.

issues.situation: (a) uses threat = max(enemy OC in range, COORD-5 centroid one-move OC). In this engine's 11e primary, rounds 1-4 score at the end of your NEXT Command phase (MissionManager.gd ~1601). That is after the enemy's whole turn (move, Advance, charge, consolidate). The base already measures this for held_threatened objectives as enemy_oc + _ri_enemy_next_move_oc (RI-RACE, nearest-model reach, line 9641). LONE-TRIP also sums: enemy_oc + projected (line 10292). Round 3's REINFORCE-CAP was dropped for this kind of undercount. Example: two CG squads (20) plus Prosecutors hold the centre, one enemy CG squad (10) is in range and another is 8" away. (a) releases a 10-OC squad (14 > 10), but the enemy can stand there with 20 before we score.
issues.proposed_change: Rounds 1-4: threat = enemy_oc + the RI-RACE next-move OC (ri_threat_by_obj; compute it if it is not cached). Round 5 (end-of-turn scoring): use only the enemy OC in range.

issues.situation: After (a) releases unit A from objective X, pass 2.5 (COORD-4) can convert another holder B on X to ATTACK. Custodian Guard, Blade Champions and Allarus are melee seekers. This happens when an enemy is within about 10-12" and no enemy centroid is on the marker. The re-opened need uses h_left = friendly_oc - B (line 10645), which still counts A's OC. So the re-open is too small or 0, nobody backfills, and X keeps only what is left after both A and B leave.
issues.proposed_change: In pass 2.5, set h_left = friendly_oc - moc_freed_oc[a_oid] - B's OC (including leaders), so the re-opened need includes OC that was already released.

issues.situation: (a) releases holders in global score order. reviews.summary:
Verdict: drop.

1. **Part (a) flips its main finding only through an OC counting bug.** At s7475 the released Custodian Guard Beta carries an attached Blade Champion (OC 2) that the design counts as staying. Rebuilt from the save with the engine's hosting-area test, obj_center is 20 (Beta 9 + Champion 2 + Gamma 9) vs 9 enemy OC in range, plus 7 more one move away. Only 9 stays, which ties. With correct counting the design's own rule keeps Beta on the objective. The stated root cause ("OC that changes no control") is also wrong here: the measured +8.0 is a trade of centre control for flipping obj_nml_1. In real games leaders are always attached, so the rule as written will leave held_threatened objectives tied or lost. The bench has no leaders and cannot see this.

2. **Part (b) mostly fires outside its own rationale.** In full games it mainly fires where the greedy pick cannot cover the need, so the extra OC is not surplus. At s7478 it sends the unit to an objective nobody measured, and the measured alternative did not confirm at horizon 2.

3. **Bench reach is below the v2 gate.** The designer's pair gave 1 line in 2 identical games. I estimate 0.3-0.7 lines per game, and less after the needed corrections.

Once corrected, the design fixes no measured finding and cannot reach the bench, so there is nothing to ship. The leader-counting gap also exists in base KEEP-OC and deserves its own audit.

issues.situation: Part (a) does not count attached Leaders. `_marginal_oc_holder_surplus` (patched AIDecisionMaker.gd ~12252) and `moc_freed_oc` subtract `cand.unit_oc`. That value comes from `_unit_alive_oc`, which counts only the bodyguard's own models. `friendly_oc` also includes attached CHARACTER units, and those move with the bodyguard: MovementPhase rejects them as separate movers and `_move_attached_characters` moves them along. The s7475 r3 P1 save shows the effect. obj_center friendly 20 = Custodian Guard Gamma 9 (already moved) + Custodian Guard Beta 9 + Blade Champion C 2 (attached to Beta). Enemy has 9 in range (Custodian Guard A_P2 has 2 models in range = 6, Custodian Guard C_P2 = 3) and 7 one move away. The log says '11 stays vs threat 9', but the 11 includes the Blade Champion that leaves with Beta, so 9 actually stays against 9 enemy: a tie. Under the design's own rule (stays > threat) Beta must hold. The flagship decision check passes only because of this miscount. The same miscount hits s7477 r3 P2: if Custodian Guard Delta (with Blade Champion A_P2 attached) is processed first, the helper computes 5 > 3, but 3 vs 3 actually remains. It also affects every real game with Leaders. The bench fixtures have no attachments, so the bench cannot detect it.
issues.proposed_change: Compute the departing OC as the unit's in-range OC plus the in-range OC of each id in its attachment_data.attached_characters (`_unit_oc_at_position` with hd_obj_by_id/hd_mm). Use that value for both `stays` and `moc_freed_oc`. Add a test with a Leader-attached holder. Note: after this change s7475 no longer fires (9 is not > 9), so the design loses its main finding.

issues.situation: Pass 2.5 (COORD-4 attack conversion, patched file ~10686-10687) computes `h_left = friendly_oc - unit_oc`, so it still counts the OC of holders that (a) freed. Example: on a held_threatened objective, (a) frees holder X because holder Y 'stays'. Y is a melee seeker (bench Custodian Guard, Allarus and Blade Champions all are). On the bench's large 11e terrain objectives Y's centroid is often more than 3.79" from the marker, so the gate's 'stays on contested objective' exit does not apply, and Y can be converted to ATTACK. Its re-open check then sees X's OC as still present, re-opens 0 need, and there is no backfill. The objective is left with less OC than the threat. On the base this cannot happen on held_threatened objectives because every holder holds.
issues.proposed_change: When marginal_oc_on, subtract `moc_freed_oc.get(a_oid, 0)` from `h_left` in the pass-2.5 hold branch. Alternatively, make the (a) release final only after pass 2.5, re-checked against the finished plan, as KEEPER-RELEASE does after pass 3. Add a test where the remaining holder is chase-gated.

issues.situation: The threat measure is max(enemy OC in range, enemy OC one move away), taken from KEEP-OC. KEEP-OC runs on held_safe objectives, where enemy_oc is about 0, so max and sum are nearly equal there. On held_threatened objectives the two differ. The measure also misses the out-of-range models of enemy units that are partly in range (projected_enemy_oc skips such units), Advance reach, and engaged friendly holders that may Fall Back. At s7475 the enemy can bring 9 + 7 + 3 = 19 OC against the 9 that stays. This is round 3's REINFORCE-CAP failure mode: the threat count missed enemy units that could still reach the objective.
issues.proposed_change: Use threat = enemy_oc + projected_enemy_oc (lone_trip_oc's measure) plus the out-of-range OC of enemy units that are partly in range. Count only non-engaged holders as 'stays'.

issues.situation: Part (a) ignores an authored plan's HOLD_OBJECTIVE earmark. KEEPER-RELEASE explicitly keeps such a unit, and the shipped Orks plans use the earmark (40k/data/ai_plans/orks_free_grab_grip_hammer_anvil.json, recon_stomps). A plan-ordered holder on a surplus held_threatened objective is freed and sent elsewhere. There is no bench effect because the bench runs without plans.
issues.proposed_change: Skip (a) when `str(cand.get("earmark", "")).begins_with("HOLD_OBJECTIVE")`.

issues.situation: The unit that (a) frees is simply the first holder in candidate score order, i.e. the one with the highest hold score. It is not the holder whose OC would change control elsewhere (no best_elsewhere or KEEPER-PICK logic). A freed unit that pass 2 cannot place falls to pass-3 support or screening and can leave the threatened objective for nothing. The designer's one bench fire (Prosecutors, obj_home_1) changed no action: both games had 681 actions and pair E was 0.0.

issues.situation: Part (b) is a proxy. At s7478 it fires on 9 vs 8 OC, although both units far exceed the need of 1. reviews.summary: Drop. The design's main claim is that the AI credits OC 'that changes no control'. The s7475 save contradicts this. Custodian Guard Beta's Blade Champion C (OC 2) is attached and leaves with it, so freeing Beta leaves 9 vs 9 enemy in range (a tie), not the '11 stays' in the log. With the enemy's full potential (9 in range + 7 one move away + 3 from a partly-in-range unit) the margin is gone. A second real bug: pass 2.5 can turn the 'staying' holder into an attacker without re-opening any need, because its h_left still counts the freed OC. It sends Custodian Guard Beta on an unmeasured ~24\" trip to obj_nml_1, not the measured centre move. Bench reach is 0.5/game on the one fixture measured, and that fire changed nothing. A revision that fixes the bugs (Leader OC, sum threat, pass-2.5 re-open, HOLD_OBJECTIVE earmark) gives a sound but rarely-firing surplus rule with no measured support for this cluster. issues.situation: The threat model misses enemy OC that can arrive by moving onto the objective's terrain area, by Advancing, or by consolidating after a fight. This repeats round 3's REINFORCE-CAP lesson. Every objective in the 3 bench fixtures is a terrain-hosted area (home and no-man's-land 7"x11.5", centre 11.6"x10"). Yet _marginal_oc_free_projected_oc copies COORD-5's test (unit centroid to MARKER within M+2"+3.79"), ignores Advance, and drops every engaged enemy unit. Evidence: (a) At s7475, one Allarus P2 model is 6.7" from the centre's area (M7), but the unit's centroid is 16.4" from the marker, so it is not counted. BC C P2 and BC B P2 (2.2" and 2.8" from the area) are excluded as engaged, but their only engaged partner is our lone Blade Champion B (bodyguard dead, engaged with 4 enemy units). When it dies, 11e 12.08 Objective Consolidation lets them move onto the centre. (b) At s7420 r3 P2, the design counts no walk-in OC (threat 0-2, margin 7-9), so it frees Custodian Guard C, the very move measured at -4.75 [-11.12, 1.62] over 12 seeds. In fact one Thunderwolf Cavalry model plus the Chaplain on Bike can move onto the area (4 OC; 6 OC with an Advance, margin 1). The Allarus can then also be freed (margin 3 after CG C). (c) I emulated the design's rule over all 262 unique saved movement phases. Its release condition holds in 6 holder checks; in 4 of the 6, the margin drops below 2 once enemy models that can Advance onto the hosting area are counted per model (3 of 6 with Normal moves only).
issues.proposed_change: Count the walk-in threat per model with MissionManager.model_gap_to_objective_range_px: gap at most M for a Normal move, at most M+3.5" for units that can Advance. Also count an engaged enemy unit within 3" of the objective or area when its only engaged partners are single-model or fragile units (12.08 consolidation). Require a margin of at least the largest per-model OC among the remaining holders plus 1, so that one casualty cannot turn the objective into a tie (ties give no control in MissionManager).

issues.situation: An attached leader's OC is not subtracted when its bodyguard leaves. left_oc removes only the bodyguard's own models. An attached character is never in movable_units (MovementPhase rejects it with 'Attached character moves with its bodyguard unit') and leaves with the bodyguard. Real games attach leaders: the AI pairs Blade Champions with Custodian Guard at deployment, 3 of 4 Custodian Guard units in the custodes_lions games. At s7475, Blade Champion C (OC 2) is attached to Beta. The true OC left is 9 against 9 enemy in range: a tie, margin 0, not the logged '11 OC left'. issues.proposed_change: Subtract the in-range OC of every unit in attachment_data.attached_characters, and add it to moc_released_oc. Add a unit test with an attached leader. Expect s7475 to stop changing, and report that honestly.

issues.situation: The release is not tied to the target that justified it. MOC-HOLD frees a holder in pass 1 if any objective within 2 turns that we do not hold still needs OC, even when the unit's OC cannot change control there (at s7420, obj_nml_1 needs 11 and CG C brings 9). Pass 2 then assigns the freed unit in global score order. It can take a 3+-turn or lost-race trip. If another unit fills the target first, it falls to the pass-3 support fallback, which may send it back or to another held objective. Unlike KEEPER-RELEASE, there is no check after the passes. The [MARGINAL_OC] line prints in pass 1, so reach counts include releases that change nothing.
issues.proposed_change: Require unit OC plus OC already planned there to be at least the target's need. After pass 3, restore the hold unless the freed unit's final order is a move or advance, within MARGINAL_OC_MAX_TURNS, to an objective where its OC changes control. Print the tag only after that check.

issues.situation: Which holder is freed depends on candidate score order. Hold scores carry the horde bonus, so the biggest squad is checked and freed first, whatever its durability or points. In the bench Custodes list that can free a Custodian Guard and leave Prosecutors (T3, W1, OC 8) or a lone Blade Champion as the holder, to be shot off in the enemy turn. A margin of 2 is less than one Custodian Guard model's OC.

(1) The bench cannot measure it: the designer's own Custodes pair had 0 fires and games identical to base, and I estimate at most 0.3 fires per game across the 3 fixtures. (2) Its one MOC-HOLD success, s7475, depends on two counting errors. Blade Champion C (OC 2) is attached to Beta and leaves with it, so the true OC left is 9 vs 9 in range (a tie). One Allarus P2 model is 6.7\" from the centre's terrain area, but the centroid-to-marker reach misses it. Correcting either one alone stops the release, so the rule's 'safe surplus' premise was false at the very position that measured +8. The gain there came from flipping and denying obj_nml_1 while the centre was under heavy threat, a value trade the rule never models. (3) Where the rule's condition holds in saved sweep positions (6 holder checks in 262 movement phases), 4 of 6 stop being safe once enemy Advances onto the hosting area are counted. One is s7420 r3 P2, where the same move measured -4.75 over 12 seeds. (4) The release condition never checks that the freed unit's OC changes control at its target, and pass 2 can send the unit elsewhere. (5) MOC-SWAP's s7478 choice is a different target from the measured alternative and was checked on only 8 seeds. If the cluster is revisited, the evidence points to valuing the trade (flip or denial elsewhere vs expected loss at the held objective), with a per-model, area-aware threat that includes Advance, charges and 12.08 consolidation and subtracts attached leaders, and with bench reach measured first. reviews.summary:
The code is cleanly gated and honestly reported, but it needs revision before it can be judged on its merits.
- **The flagship flip is an accounting error.** At s7475, Blade Champion C (OC 2, in range) is attached to Custodian Guard Beta and leaves with it. The centre is really left at a 9 vs 9 tie, not 11 vs 9.
- **The threat count misses an enemy.** It measures reach to the marker, so an unengaged Allarus unit (OC 6) 6.7" from the centre's hosting area is not counted.
- **Either fix alone holds Beta.** The +8.00 measured at s7475 is therefore a trade that the design's own surplus rule would refuse, not evidence for the rule.
- **Pass 2.5 uses a stale ledger.** It re-opens needs without subtracting the holders MOC-HOLD freed.
- **MOC-SWAP is sound but thinly supported.** It fires at s7478, but sends Beta to obj_nml_1, which only the designer's 8-seed run supports. Guardrails s7457 r1 P2 and the new s7489 r1 P1 have MOC-SWAP preconditions and were not replayed.
- **Bench reach is about 0.** That was measured on the Custodes fixture and follows from M6 Custodes, so the design will likely PARK at the v2 fix gate.

To revise:
1. Count attached characters as leaving with the holder.
2. Use `_ri_enemy_next_move_oc` (hosting-area gap) for the walk-on threat.
3. Fix the pass-2.5 ledger.
4. Replay s7475, s7478, all 7 guardrails and s7489, and measure reach on all 3 fixtures.

verdict.reasons:
No design is both safe and measurable, so there is no winner. I verified the following myself from code at 12e0753 and the decoded saves; I did not run Godot.

(1) The s7475 r3 P1 flip that all three designs claim rests on miscounted OC. Rebuilt with the hosting-area test, obj_center is Guard Beta 9 + Blade Champion C 2 + Guard Gamma 9 against 9 enemy OC. The save's attachment_data shows Champion C attached to Beta. friendly_oc counts the Champion as a separate unit, but it moves with Beta, so releasing Beta leaves 9 against 9, a tie. All three rules count it as staying: narrow's locked_oc_holds, root's _marginal_oc_holder_surplus and game's left_oc. With leader-aware counting none of them fires there. Narrow's flip is also a replay artifact: Gamma's REMAIN_STATIONARY carried the plan entry, and COORD-4 builds the plan once per phase, so at the real plan locked OC was 2. The measured +8.00 is a value trade (a tied centre for an obj_nml_1 flip), and none of the rules models that trade.

(2) Because the count ignores leaders, every (a) gate can tie or empty a held_threatened objective in real games, where the AI attaches every Blade Champion (confirmed in the sweep saves). The bench cannot catch this: I checked all 3 fixtures and they have 0 attachments and 0 reserves. Analogue positions where a surplus release would fire lean negative (s7420 -4.75, s7477 -1.92, both n12).

(3) What survives is the (b) swap gate. It really flips s7478 r3 P2, because that swap came from the phase-start plan. But it sends Beta to obj_nml_1 (+9.13/+9.25, n8), not the measured centre move. Root's form of (b) is also wrong where the greedy pick cannot cover the need.

(4) Bench reach fails the v2 fix gate on the data we have: narrow 0 tag lines in 8 bench games; game 0 in its pair; root 0.5/game in 1 Custodes pair, and that fire changed no action. The Orks mirror was not measured for any design.

The ranking puts game first (the most guarded, best tested), then narrow (smallest, best (b), but its flagship result is invalid and gate (a) frees all holders at once), then root (its reach comes from the least guarded release, and its (b) works against its own rationale).
